$comment: GNU LOCAL REGISTER VARIABLES bound to the inline-asm operands that read and write them (D-C-LOCAL-REGISTER-VARIABLE-ASM-LABEL-IGNORED, D-ASM-MATCHING-CONSTRAINT-DIGIT-READ-AS-A-MACHINE-LETTER), on all four shipped targets. Every template names its register BY NAME, so a dropped binding reads the wrong register and exits 11–18 (one code per shape; `main.c` lists them). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-19, each reference SEPARATELY at -O0 and -O2: gcc 13.3.0 runs it to 42 on x86_64 and aarch64 (qemu), and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 on the PE target; clang 18.1.3 runs it to 42 on aarch64 at -O2, refuses x86_64 shape E (it binds no two-register value there) and dies at aarch64 -O0 in shape F (it copies the never-written variable's indeterminate slot into sp — removing F alone turns that crash into 42). The P68 round-7 base REFUSED this file (`S_InlineAsmConstraintLetterUndeclared`: it read the matching constraint `"0"` as a machine letter), and compiled each binding shape ALONE at rc=0 with its value wherever the allocator put it — the wrong answer at debug and release unless the allocator happened to choose the named register. ★ Shape F reads the stack pointer through a variable that is never written — the register AS IT STANDS — and shape H binds the aarch64 LINK register in a leaf, which must then save it. ★ The `release` arm keeps every seed `volatile`, so each bound register is still loaded from a value the optimizer cannot fold. ⓘ Mach-O arm64 binds no x18 (Apple reserves it) and no x29.
